valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E (FY2027 non-GAAP diluted EPS viewed at the 12-month target date, Nov 2027). FY2026 non-GAAP EPS is derived, not guided: Q1 2026 $1.91, Q2 2026 $2.93 and Q3 2026 $2.95 sum to $7.79 for nine months; adding a Q4 2026 estimate of about $4.75 (Q4 2025 was $4.52, grown about 5%, an assumption) gives about $12.54. IBM gives no full-year EPS guidance; it reiterated 4-5% constant-currency revenue growth and raised free cash flow growth to more than $1 billion. Base FY2027 EPS of $13.40 is about 7% growth on the derived FY2026 figure and sits near the sourced FY2027 consensus of about $13.30 (spring 2026, so stale). IBM trades as NYSE common stock priced in USD, so no ADR ratio or FX conversion applies. Share count is about 0.945 billion (pipeline aggregate). Dividends are excluded from the price targets.

bear.driver: Revenue growth slips toward the low end of the 4-5% guide as software and consulting growth fades; the Q3 2026 pre-tax margin gain (19.3%, +70 bp) does not carry into 2027; the multiple de-rates as growth disappoints
bear.assumption: FY2027 EPS $12.60 (about flat on derived FY2026 EPS of $12.54) x 16x

base.driver: Revenue grows about 4-5% with non-GAAP pre-tax margin continuing to expand, supporting about 7% EPS growth; the multiple holds near 19x, close to the current forward multiple

bull.driver: Software and hybrid cloud growth re-accelerates and margin expansion continues; EPS grows about 13%; the multiple re-rates to 22x as growth visibility improves

valuation.implied_by_close: At base FY2027 EPS of $13.40 the $247.13 close implies 18.4x; at derived FY2026 EPS of $12.54 it implies 19.7x. The mean of the four named post-earnings targets (Oct 22, 2026: $260, $277, $243, $280) is $265.0, which implies 19.8x base EPS, or $13.95 of EPS at 19x (4.1% above base). The pipeline aggregate mean of $259.85 (23 analysts, Yahoo Finance via yfinance) implies 19.4x base EPS.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $13.40 (5.4 pp of the close). A $0.10 change in FY2027 base EPS moves the base target by $1.90 (0.8 pp).
valuation.watch_metric: Software and consulting revenue growth staying inside the 4-5% constant-currency guide, with non-GAAP pre-tax margin expansion (Q3 2026 19.3%) carrying into FY2027. Revenue growth below 4% or a margin that stalls would break the base case.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 and FY2026 results with FY2027 commentary, expected late January 2027 (date not confirmed in the sources reviewed).

analyst_notes: Twelve named analysts have dated calls in the last nine months, but only four are post-earnings: Stifel (Grossman, $260, Buy), Barclays (Lenschow, $277, Overweight), UBS (Vogt, $243, Neutral) and Jefferies (Thill, $280, Buy), all dated Oct 22, 2026. Their $265.0 mean sits 4.1% above our $254.60 base, which needs roughly $13.95 of FY2027 EPS at 19x or a multiple near 20x. Older named targets are much higher (Oppenheimer $380 from Jan 29, Wedbush $320 from Apr 23) and Morgan Stanley's $215 from Apr 14 and HSBC's $175 from Jul 16 are lower, so the named sample is wide ($175-$380) and the older targets are stale. No named target has a documented 12-month horizon, so no weighted target is computed; the rating and target histories are sourced from one aggregator table that gives no prior values, and the firm-level rating rows are attached to the named analysts dated the same day.
